title: Uniform vanishing of Ext between integral constructible sheaves
statement:
Work in the global finite-field setting of [sk-def-sf-setting]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$, $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaves and the categories $\Cons(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $L$ be as in [det-lem-int-ext-formula](1): $i$ is closed, $u$ is open, and $L\in\Cons(S,\mathcal O_E)$ is pro-étale locally the completion of a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module, possibly with torsion. Let $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the open complement of $i$, and use the cohomological dimensions of [sk-def-cd]. Then
$$
\Ext^r_X(a_!L,N)=0\qquad\text{for }r>\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+3
\quad\text{and every }N\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E).
$$
Here $\Ext^r_X(A,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)}(A,N[r])$.
Consequently every $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ has an integer $d_C\ge0$ with $\Ext^r_X(C,N)=0$ for $r>d_C$ and every $N\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put $c=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)$ and $s=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$. The base field is algebraically closed, so its $\ell$-cohomological dimension is zero by [sk-lem-base-field-cd]. The schemes $S,Z,X\setminus Z$ are finite type over $k$, and $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion between Noetherian schemes. Thus the finiteness assertion of [sk-def-cd] gives finite nonnegative integers $c,s$. We use $B_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $A_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_T$ for each scheme $T$.

source.place: unit proof, third paragraph: finiteness of the two cohomological dimensions

proof.text: Fix $N\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$. By [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](1), $N[0]\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Apply [sk-lem-integral-models](2): $N$ is derived complete and its first reduction is bounded constructible of étale origin. Define the actual derived reductions $N_n=N\otimes^L_{B_X}A_{n,X}$ with their canonical quotient transitions, all viewed also as $B_X$-complexes by restriction of scalars. The complete-reduction criterion [det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions] makes every $N_n$ bounded constructible. By [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] each is classical, that is, of étale origin. Derived completeness, as stated in [sk-lem-integral-models], gives $N\simeq R\varprojlim_n N_n$. No separate choice of compatible complexes is needed: the quotient maps define the tower functorially.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Lemmas 6.5.3--6.5.4; unit proof, third paragraph; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion) for reconstruction

proof.text: The finite free resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. Its completed sheaf version still resolves $A_{n,X}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. Tensoring this bounded free model with $N[0]$ represents the underlying $B_X$-complex $N_n$ by $[N\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}N]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. Hence $H^r(N_n)=0$ outside $[-1,0]$. Its $A_{n,X}$-module structure is the one on the derived reduction, so its cohomology is killed by $\pi_E^n$, and therefore by a power of $\ell$. This checks the torsion hypothesis of the cohomological dimension bounds, including for torsion $N$.

Use the derived dual $D=R\mathcal Hom_{B_S}(L,B_S)$, not ordinary sheaf Hom. By [sk-lem-int-integral-heart](3), $L$ is dualizable and $D$ has Tor amplitude $[0,1]$. For every $B_S$-complex $M$, evaluation and coevaluation give mutually inverse maps
$$R\mathcal Hom_{B_S}(L,M)\simeq D\otimes^L_{B_S}M.$$
Indeed, the forward transpose uses $1\to L\otimes D$ followed by evaluation $L\otimes R\mathcal Hom(L,M)\to M$; the inverse is the transpose of $D\otimes L\otimes M\to M$. Their composites are identities by the two duality triangle identities, using [def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction-modules]. The closed-support adjunction of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support](1), and $u_!\dashv u^*$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], give
$$\Ext^r_X(a_!L,K)=H^rR\Gamma(S,D\otimes^L_{B_S}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK).$$
Here the open adjunction derives by [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]; both open functors are exact by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so their derived functors equal their termwise functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. The final identification with hypercohomology is [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], applied also after shift by $r$. This derives the formula needed here with the derived dual. It agrees with the now corrected clause (2) of [det-lem-int-ext-formula]; the imported blueprint and unit paragraph 1 used an incorrect ordinary dual.

source.place: Tags 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U); unit proof, first paragraph, corrected to the derived dual

proof.text: Let $D_n=D\otimes^L_{B_S}A_{n,S}$. It has Tor amplitude $[0,1]$ over $A_{n,S}$: for an $A_{n,S}$-module $F$, associativity gives $D_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,S}}F=D\otimes^L_{B_S}F$, to which step 4 applies. Also $D_n$ is bounded constructible. Work on each pro-\'etale trivializing object $V\to S$ from the local-model hypothesis, so that $L|_V\simeq B_V\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P$ for a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module $P$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR. Choose a finite free surjection $\mathcal O_E^v\twoheadrightarrow P$. Its kernel is finite free by [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form], since it is a submodule of the finite free source. This gives a two-term finite free resolution of $P$. The flatness of $B_V$ over the constant $\mathcal O_E$ sheaf from [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] makes its completed extension a local bounded finite-free model of $L|_V$, with matrices over $\mathcal O_E$. The termwise dual model, with reversed degrees and dual differentials, is a dual by evaluation on each finite-free term; the tensor-Hom transpose and the two triangle identities of step 4 identify it with $D|_V$. Reducing its matrices modulo $\pi_E^n$ gives a bounded finite-free constant local model for $D_n|_V$. Its cohomology is locally constant with finite $A_n$-module values, since $A_n$ is finite; boundedness in $[0,1]$ was already checked by the Tor-amplitude assertion. Thus [sk-def-sfb-constructible] gives constructibility, and [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives classicality of $D_n$. Change of coefficients and its tensor comparison are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the identity topos with ring map $B_S\to A_{n,S}$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), termwise dual of a strictly perfect model; finite-coefficient constructible comparison, Tag 099Y

proof.text:
First check that finite-coefficient direct images compute the integral direct images used in step 4. Write $F_T=-\otimes^L_{B_T}A_{n,T}$ and $U_T=\operatorname{Res}_n$. By [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction], $F_T\dashv U_T$, with $U_T$ exact. For $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, the derived geometric adjunction is [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and the tensor pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives $F_Vj_B^*\simeq j_A^*F_X$. Explicitly, on K-flat representatives both composites send $W$ to $A_{n,V}\otimes^L_{j^{-1}B_X}j^{-1}W$: the coefficient maps of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify $j^{-1}B_X=B_V$ and $j^{-1}A_{n,X}=A_{n,V}$, and tensor associativity cancels the intermediate $j^{-1}B_X$-extension. This identifies the two pullbacks with the same quotient maps. Thus, naturally in $W\in D(B_X)$ and $Q\in D(A_{n,V})$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(W,Rj_{B,*}U_VQ)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_V}(j_B^*W,U_VQ)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{n,V}}(F_Vj_B^*W,Q)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{n,X}}(F_XW,Rj_{A,*}Q)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(W,U_XRj_{A,*}Q).$$
These adjunction bijections identify $Rj_{B,*}U_VQ$ with $U_XRj_{A,*}Q$, including the unit maps (both transpose the identity of the restricted object). Exact geometric inverse images also commute with the coefficient-forgetting $U_T$ on the underlying sheaves. This permits the fibre and restriction calculations below at finite coefficients, then restriction of scalars back to $B$.

We bound $Rj_*j^*N_n$ with the finite coefficient ring $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. By [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], restriction of a classical complex is classical, and $Rj_*$ on bounded-below classical complexes is obtained from étale direct image. On a classical $A_n$-module sheaf $F$, the definition of $c$ in [sk-def-cd] says the underlying abelian $R^t j_*F$ vanishes for $t>c$. The module-to-abelian direct-image comparison [det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology](3) and the étale/pro-étale comparison identify this with the same assertion for module-valued derived direct image. Filter the bounded complex $j^*N_n$ by its two cohomology sheaves in degrees $-1,0$, using [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Applying $Rj_*$ preserves the triangles and shifts by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The long exact cohomology sequences of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] show that the contributions have upper bounds $c-1,c$, respectively, hence $Rj_*j^*N_n$ has upper bound $c$. It is bounded below and classical by the same direct-image comparison. Its lower bound is $-1$: the module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], applied to the small sites in a common larger universe. The direct image $j_*$ is additive and left exact because it is a right adjoint, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] says its bounded-below right derived functor preserves every lower cohomological bound.

By [sk-lem-formal-closed-support](1),
$$M_n:=u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZN_n=u^*i^*\operatorname{fib}(N_n\to Rj_*j^*N_n).$$
The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives upper bound $c+1$ for the fibre: at degree $r>c+1$, both $H^{r-1}(Rj_*j^*N_n)$ and $H^r(N_n)$ vanish. Its lower bound is $-1$, since both $N_n$ and $Rj_*j^*N_n$ are zero below $-1$. Inverse images $i^*,u^*$ are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], hence preserve these cohomological bounds by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. For classicality, represent $N_n$ on the étale site by step 2. By [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] the unit and its direct image comparison form the same fibre after exact pullback from the étale site; this pullback also commutes with $i^*,u^*$. Thus $M_n$ is classical and has cohomology in $[-1,c+1]$, with its natural $A_{n,S}$-module structure.

source.place: Tag 09A6 (lemma-morphism-comparison); unit proof, third paragraph, first bullet

proof.text: Form $T_n=D\otimes^L_{B_S}M_n=D_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,S}}M_n$; the equality is derived tensor associativity with the quotient coefficient action. Its cohomology has upper bound $c+2$. Indeed, the finite truncation triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] filter $M_n$ by $H^t(M_n)[-t]$ for $-1\le t\le c+1$. Tensoring each sheaf with $D_n$ puts cohomology in $[0,1]$ by step 5, so the shifted contribution has upper bound $t+1\le c+2$. Tensor preserves these triangles: choose K-flat models as in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; total tensor with the fixed model carries a mapping cone to the cone of the tensor map, with the same two summands and differential. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the asserted bound by finite induction. The same argument gives lower bound $-1$. Both factors are classical and bounded below. The derived unit hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] is supplied by [sk-prop-sf-comparison] for the discrete ring $A_n$. Hence that equivalence represents them as pullbacks of bounded-below étale complexes. The étale representative of $D_n$ is bounded constructible by step 5 and [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison]; [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] reflects its Tor amplitude $[0,1]$. Applying the same finite cohomology-filtration argument on the étale site makes its tensor with the étale representative of $M_n$ bounded below (in fact in $[-1,c+2]$). The tensor pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] expresses $T_n$ as the pullback of their derived tensor. Since $T_n$ is bounded, it is a bounded classical $A_{n,S}$-complex. This argument uses no constructibility assertion for $Rj_*j^*N_n$.

source.place: Tags 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); unit proof, third paragraph, second bullet

proof.text: Now apply $R\Gamma(S,-)$ to the finite cohomology filtration of $T_n$. Each $H^t(T_n)$ is classical and killed by a power of $\ell$. The definition of $s$ in [sk-def-cd], the derived sections comparison [sk-prop-sf-comparison], and the module/abelian cohomology comparison [det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology](2), give $H^v(S,H^t(T_n))=0$ for $v>s$. The truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] and the exactness and shift compatibility of $R\Gamma$ [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], together with [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], give upper bound $t+s$ for each shifted contribution and thus upper bound $c+s+2$ for $R\Gamma(S,T_n)$. Substituting this into the corrected formula from step 4 proves $\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,N_n[r])=0$ for $r>c+s+2$, uniformly in $n$ and $N$. The finite-coefficient sections bound is also the integral-coefficient bound in step 4: $F_S(B_S)=A_{n,S}$, so [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{B_S}(B_S,U_ST_n[r])=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_{n,S}}(A_{n,S},T_n[r])$. By [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and the tensor unit these are respectively the two hypercohomology groups in degree $r$. Thus no equality of module-valued and underlying abelian derived functors is being assumed for the completed ring.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle); unit proof, third paragraph, third bullet

proof.text:
Put $b=c+s+2$ and $P=\prod_{n\ge1}N_n$ in $D(B_X)$. This product exists by [det-pe-products-derived]. Step 2 and [def-weil-derived-limit] give a distinguished Roos triangle $N\to P\xrightarrow{1-t}P\to N[1]$. By the product universal property and the shift equivalence,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,P[r])\cong\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,N_n[r])=0\quad(r>b).$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to this triangle, shifted by $r-1$. Exactness at $\operatorname{Hom}(a_!L,N[r])$ says every map to $N[r]$ factors through $P[r-1]$ when its composite to $P[r]$ is zero. For $r>b+1$, both groups of maps into $P[r-1]$ and $P[r]$ are zero, so every map to $N[r]$ is zero. This proves the required $c+s+3$ bound. It is exactly the one-degree loss of the Milnor argument, without needing limits to commute with any immersion inverse-image functor.

source.place: Tags 08TC (definition-derived-limit), 08TB (section-derived-limit), Hom exact sequence into the Roos triangle

proof.text: For $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ use only clause (1) of [det-lem-int-ext-formula]: there is a finite filtration by distinguished triangles with pieces $a_{\alpha,!}L_\alpha$ in degree zero. Let $d_C$ be the maximum of the finitely many integers $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j_\alpha)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S_\alpha)+3$, taking $d_0=0$ for the empty filtration. For fixed $N$ and $r>d_C$, every piece has zero maps to $N[r]$ by step 10. At each filtration triangle $C'\to C''\to a_{\alpha,!}L_\alpha\to C'[1]$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i) gives exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(a_{\alpha,!}L_\alpha,N[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C'',N[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C',N[r])$. Its outside groups are zero, so the middle group is zero. Induction from the zero object proves the assertion for $C$. The bound is independent of $N$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N4-021b7dcd1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the whole item. The delivery is one commit with the item and its report; it adds no new nodes, proof_deps is exactly the union of the step uses, and no SGA source is cited. Statement: both clauses and the bound cd(j)+cd(S)+3 are kept, and torsion L is still allowed. The one change is that the setting is now k = F̄_q. This is justified: the only citer, sk-lem-int-ext, has sk-def-sf-setting in its stmt_deps, and over an arbitrary field of characteristic p the integer d_C can fail when cd_l(k) is infinite. The report names the change. All 11 steps check out against the cited statements. (1) cd_l(k)=0 and Tag 0F10 give finite c and s. (2) sk-lem-integral-models(2), the reductions criterion and the constructible comparison make every N_n classical with N = R lim N_n (Stacks 099M, Bhatt-Scholze Def. 6.5.1 and Lemmas 6.5.3-6.5.4). (3) N_n is the cone of pi^n on N, with cohomology in [-1,0] killed by pi^n. (4) The formula uses the derived dual RHom(L,B_S), dualizable with Tor amplitude [0,1]; the closed-support adjunction applies because O_E is an admissible coefficient. I confirmed the worker's counterexample to the old ordinary dual (Ext^1(O_E/pi,O_E)=O_E/pi), and the result agrees with the corrected clause (2) of det-lem-int-ext-formula. (5) A local finite-free model, built with the DVR and Smith normal form, makes D_n constructible and classical with Tor amplitude [0,1]. (6) The adjunction chain gives Rj_{B*}Res = Res Rj_{A*}, and Rj_*j^*N_n lies in [-1,c]. (7) M_n lies in [-1,c+1] and is classical. (8) T_n lies in [-1,c+2] and is classical. (9) RGamma(S,T_n) has upper bound c+s+2. (10) Hom into the Roos triangle (Stacks 08TC) gives c+s+3, the unit's one-degree loss, without needing Tag 09AA. (11) The finite filtration with Hom-out-of-triangle exactness gives d_C, with d_0=0. Small cases checked: S empty, Z=X, and a point with L=O_E or L=O_E/pi. The det-uniform-constructible-ext-* nodes and sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext are not duplicates. I accept all declared tool_uses as generic tools. No fixes made. Minor, not faults: source.external still lists the blueprint's 099Q and 08TB, and step 4 re-derives the sibling formula instead of citing it.
